data.title: Grain Futures Finish Mixed to End Shaky Week for Commodities — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

--Corn for March delivery fell 0.8% Friday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $4.48 3/4 a bushel, closing out a negative week for commodities with losses.

--Wheat for March delivery declined 0.5% to $5.92 a bushel.

--Soybeans for January delivery rose 1.1% to $12.20 3/4 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

No Risk Premium: Grains trading is likely to remain choppy in the short term as markets tussle with currency issues, South American weather and changes in global trade flows with no Russia-Ukraine peace deal likely, AgResource said in a note. "ARC maintains there's little to no risk premium in grains markets currently, and the assumption is that geopolitics and South American weather progress smoothly through the balance of 2026," the firm said. They also added that it won't take much in the way of shifting grain flows or weather scares in South America to give prices a boost.

Forecast Tweak: The International Grains Council raised its 2026/27 global production estimate for wheat and coarse grains by 1 million metric tons to 2.428 billion tons, with higher wheat and barley numbers offsetting lower corn. The biggest changes were increases for Turkey, Australia and Argentina, and a reduction for the U.S., the IGC says. Ending grain stocks are raised by 7 million tons to 626 million tons, "inflated by unusually heavy inventories in Russia and Ukraine." Soybean production is seen at 439 million tons, unchanged from the October forecast.

Flash Sale: The USDA reported sales of 100,000 metric tons of soybean cake and meal for delivery to Spain during the 2026/2027 marketing year.

INSIGHT

Bears vs. Bulls: Corn futures typically rise between Thanksgiving and year-end, with the March contract making an average gain of 32 cents a bushel between Nov. 20 and Dec. 31 in the past 12 years, Naomi Blohm of Total Farm Marketing said in a note.

"The old expression for grains: 'the bears get Thanksgiving, but the bulls get Christmas' may have rung true with the lower price action this November," she said. While each year has its own fundamental supply and demand perspectives, the March contract has had some sort of rally during the period since 2014. Some lasted only days, but others stretched to weeks.

Looking Up: Citi Research maintains a positive view on a number of agricultural commodities including corn and soybeans, and sees the recent drawdown as a buying opportunity. "We still expect El Niño to have larger impact on yields in the next 3-6 months," global head of commodities research Max Layton said in a note. Markets will also start taking notice of the Black Sea closure as Ukraine typically ramps up exports during this time of year. "Exports of both corn and soy have been relatively strong and we expect China delivering on their commitments on buying U.S. soy and potentially corn," Layton added.

AHEAD

--The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.

--The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.

--The USDA will release its monthly Cold Storage report at 3 p.m. ET Tuesday .

--The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday

data.title: SEC Proposes to Bring Securities Reporting Platform Under Direct Supervision
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Securities and Exchange Commission is proposing to restructure the system where securities exchanges report trading data.

The proposal aims to change the Consolidated Audit Trail, which is a centralized database that tracks trading activity across securities exchanges.

The SEC has proposed to rescind Rule 613, which requires securities exchanges to report their trading activity to the CAT. In its place, the SEC proposes to require exchanges to report the same information directly to the SEC or its designee.

The move would bring the CAT under the SEC's direct control.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins has been reviewing the CAT and approving amendments that have reduced its annual operating costs by more than $100 million. Atkins has also permanently eliminated the reporting of personally identifiable information to the CAT.

The proposal addresses concerns about the CAT's funding and would put the database on sustainable footing, Atkins said.

data.title: My husband spent $80,000 on a boat, yet says my plans for a $100,000 pottery studio are irresponsible. Who's right?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have $2.9 million in retirement accounts. That includes some money that we inherited about 10 years ago.'

"My husband, however, is skeptical. He says that's a lot of money to spend on something that I'm trying to profit from." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My husband and I have been married for 31 years. He's 65 and I'm 62. I work part-time in a dental office and we have a house that's fully paid off. It's worth about $900,000. Best of all, we have $2.9 million in retirement accounts. That includes some money that we inherited about 10 years ago.

For the last 15 years, I have dreamed of opening my own pottery studio. I've taken lessons at our Saturday market for several years, and I find it extremely meditative and also a wonderful pastime. There's a space near an old rail depot, about 900 square feet, which would be perfect for a pottery studio, where I could teach others. By my estimations, insurance, equipment and rent would require about $100,000.

My husband, however, is skeptical. He says that's a lot of money to spend on something that I'm trying to profit from. My sister says it's bad timing given that we're both heading into retirement. Three years ago, he purchased a boat for $80,000 and spent $12,000 on a new motor and fishfinder. He barely used it, and finally sold it at a loss.

I'm not claiming my pottery studio will make us rich, but I'm perfectly willing to come up with a business plan and set a budget, with a red line on the amount of money I would be prepared to lose. I'd actually also start a lot smaller and build up if the price is right. We could have 30 years ahead of us in retirement, and I want to spend it doing something that brings me a lot of joy.

Am I being unrealistic?

A 62-Year-Old Wife

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I like the idea of a big return': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started.

Dear Wife,

From your letter, it doesn't sound like pottery is just a business for you.

For you, pottery is a passion, and it's important to have something you like doing in retirement. If you are going to choose to open a business, it should be something you will love because it won't always be easy, and you may need to rely on that bedrock of belief when the going gets tough. That's in addition to financial projections, advice from an accountant, knowing where you draw a hard line on the budget if sales dry up, and even a Plan B for the space.

I'm not going to tell you to open a business and spend $100,000, which could be a little on the high side, although you will know more when you compare this plan to similar-sized businesses and complete your due diligence. More important, I'm not going to tell you not to do it, and I don't think anyone else should, either, at least not without hearing you out, visiting the proposed site and, crucially, seeing your business plan. What stands out from your letter is your husband's immediate, possibly knee-jerk, opposition.

However, pointing out that he bought an $80,000 motorboat and ended up throwing good money after bad and selling it at a loss may be fair, but it doesn't help your cause. Yes, he decided to pursue something that he eventually tired of or decided wasn't worth all the hassle and expense. He's the one who apparently lost interest in a project after spending nearly six figures, not you. But it won't help to trade successes and failures in a tit-for-tat argument.

If a pottery studio is a vocation, you have earned the right to at least look into it.

It may be that you don't have to lease this building, as romantic as it sounds. You could rent a space at a retirement center or local school, at least initially, invest in the equipment to host pottery classes, build up word of mouth or an online presence and see how much demand is out there. That way, you won't be locked into a lease if the demand is not there. It will also help you envision what success means to you. Is it teaching a twice-weekly class? Or running a full-time studio?

You raise a great point when you say your retirement is not about doing nothing, or spending all of your time on the golf course or tennis court, or sitting in your garden reading - rather, it's about pursuing work that fulfills you. If pottery is a vocation for you, you have earned the right to at least look into it, given that you have worked for probably 40-plus years in jobs that helped you and your husband build a $2.9 million nest egg, even if those jobs were not your first choice.

For what it's worth, your business plan should include projected costs, including the lease, insurance, equipment, advertising, branding and marketing; projected revenue; the target market (there may be schools or senior centers nearby that would jump at the opportunity for their community to learn pottery); and, of course, the competition (find out if there are similar businesses in your area and, if so, how close they are and what they charge for classes).

Related: 'I don't want to die on the sales floor': I'm 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?

Running the numbers

You won't win this argument on statements that your husband is the proverbial pot calling the kettle black, and you may not "win" the argument at all. But you will lend more credence to your pottery studio idea through data. You have $2.9 million for retirement, a mortgage-free house worth $900,000, hardly any debt, a husband who has already retired, Social Security coming down the pike, and you continue to work part-time, although that may have to end if you set up this studio.

To put your small business in context: Startup costs of $100,000 represent 3.45% of your retirement account balance. That's not nothing, but neither is it an outrageous, extravagant risk, particularly given that this is an investment to further a pastime that brings you joy and, hopefully, makes money. What is your annual income now? What will it be in five years? What are your annual expenses? How much of your retirement is in traditional accounts versus Roth?

Another missing piece of this puzzle: Do you have a "fun money" account, an emergency fund or CDs or bonds to draw from? Otherwise, you would have to take this money from your investments. That would mean you need to take more than $100,000, because you would have to pay tax on the money you withdraw from a traditional IRA or 401(k). You would lose future investment returns (which you would ideally recoup, even if only in part, from your studio).

A $100,000 startup cost represents 3.45% of your retirement-account balance.

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started, just as you would not expect him to give up on a passion project without at least stress-testing the finances. The unspoken part of this conversation, particularly after his motorboat project, is hanging over you. It does not sound like you are asking him for permission, per se - rather, you are requesting his support, and I assume you have both contributed to your retirement fund, either as a corporate worker or a homemaker.

Agree on a maximum amount you can afford to lose on a studio. You will need working capital, particularly in the early stages, when you are building your reputation. This is an opportunity to step back and ask what you want from retirement. How do you want to spend your savings? What kind of issues require unanimous agreement? (Did you agree to the motorboat purchase, for instance?) How will you navigate such issues while respecting each other's space?

A woman named Kyla Glendenning opened up a pottery studio in Fort Lauderdale and said she had revenue of $71,000 in the first six months, but spent nearly $20,000 on Facebook advertisements. That tells me, in addition to the costs of setting up a studio, signing a lease and buying equipment, that your biggest challenges will be getting the word out that you exist. Her online tutorials and videos on social media - where I found her - also require both time and money.

Don't let anyone crack your bowls before they've even hit the kiln.

Related: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

data.title: 'GTA 6' has taken over. Is it too late to buy the developer's stock?
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Also in Weekend Reads: Full coverage of the Anthropic IPO, the 'death cross' for small-cap stocks and advice from The Moneyist

Take-Two Interactive owns Rockstar Games, the developer of the "Grand Theft Auto" series of videogames.

"Grand Theft Auto VI" was released by Rockstar Games on Thursday for the PlayStation 5 and Microsoft Xbox Series X and Series S consoles. The reviews for the latest entry in the game series - coming 13 years after the launch of "GTA V" - have been overwhelmingly positive.

So now you might wonder whether or not it is too late to make a long-term investment in Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO), which owns Rockstar Games. And it might surprise you that Take-Two's stock was down 18.5% for 2026, and had lost 8.4% for the week, through Thursday. Then again, the stock had risen 39.1% in 2025 as investors anticipated the "GTA 6" release, which was delayed.

Bill Peters looked into the reasons investors have sold-off Take-Two's stock, even as the company booked $2.36 billion in pre-orders for "GTA 6."

The sales cycle for "GTA 6" is expected to stretch over several years. While it has been released on two console platforms, Rockstar hasn't said when the game will be released on PCs.

Take-Two's stock closed at $208.65 on Thursday, and its forward price/earnings ratio was 23.6, based on the consensus 12-month earnings-per-share estimate of $8.86 among analysts polled by FactSet. That forward P/E compares with a weighted valuation of 17.3 for the S&P 500 SPX.

The stock might appear to be a bit pricey. But if we look at full-year estimates, the company's earnings per share are expected to increase at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 28.9% from calendar 2026 through 2028. And that earnings growth is expected to follow this year's profit boost from the "GTA 6" release.

The projected EPS CAGR for the S&P 500 from 2026 through 2028 is 16.9%. Per the P/E valuations, investors aren't paying a high premium for Take-Two when compared with the index.

Grand Theft Callout: 'GTA 6' fans are missing work to play - and some companies are making the game's release a holiday

The stock market's broadening decline and a series of warnings for investors and traders

What began as a sharp decline for Big Tech has spread across small-cap stocks. Tomi Kilgore explained how the current "death cross" technical pattern for the Russell 2000 Index fits in with previous market cycles.

More coverage of the markets:

-- Gold is in a bear market - and hackproof in an increasingly digital world. Is now a good time to buy?

-- How copper's plunge could hurt the AI buildout

-- Markets are sending troubling signals about the state of the economy

-- Investors are rushing back into cybersecurity stocks after a string of outages. Here's what to know before buying.

-- The stock market is being rocked by the biggest shake-up in a generation as tech falls behind

-- Has the stock market's slump hit bottom yet? Here's what these contrarian indicators say.

What's next for Anthropic?

Anthrop complete a successful initial public offering on Thursday, as its shares soared 17.1%. But the stock fell on Friday.

After pricing its initial public offering at $83 a share, Anthropic's (ANT) stock soared 17.1% to close at $97.17 on Thursday, its first day of trading.

But on Friday, Anthropic's shares were trading as low as $85, as the S&P 500's information-technology sector was down 3.9%.

William Gavin: After Anthropic's 'bittersweet' IPO, here's what lies ahead

Andrew Keshner: Anthropic is coming to your 401(k). Love it or hate it, AI is becoming a bigger part of your financial plan.

Nvidia reports solid numbers, and the stock keeps falling

Nvidia's (NVDA) stock was trading around $128 on Friday toward an 18-month low, down about 33% for November.

On Tuesday, the company announced its latest strong set of quarterly numbers. During a conference call with analysts after the market close, Harvey Jones, the chairman of Nvidia's board of directors, said the board had no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Huang, the company's co-founder, resigned on Nov. 12.

Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress raised the company's outlook for fiscal 2027 to a 75% increase in sales from the previous projection of a 70% increase. But on Wednesday the stock declined 2.9%, as investors waited to see who would be named as the company's permanent CEO.

One possible negative bellwether for the AI buildout was Kress's comment that although Nvidia would continue to provide financing for customers, the company would be "disciplined in how we commit capital," according to a transcript provided by FactSet.

Here is a sampling of related coverage:

What goes on in a buyer's market

The difficult housing market can make for happy home buyers as sellers are forced to make concessions.

Aarthi Swminathan explained how sales-contract cancellations have increased in the housing market, and what sellers are doing "to get in line with reality" to move homes.

A counterplay in the stock market

It may be difficult to summon up enthusiasm for long-term investments during a broad decline for the stock market, but Michael Brush pointed to an industry that has seen heavy insider buying. Executives are ponying up their own cash to buy their employer's stocks in the aerospace and defense industry, for which government spending is expected to balloon next year.

Building retirement accounts for your children

Wouldn't it be nice to be able to help set your children to be free from financial worries as they get older? This week in the Help Me Retire column, Alessandra Malito had advice for a self-described "plan-ahead mom" who wants to make sure her young children end up to be millionaires.

Golden Key Group Selected by the City of Cleveland to Deliver Enterprise-Wide Management Training Program

Golden Key Group Selected by the City of Cleveland to Deliver Enterprise-Wide Management Training Program

PR Newswire

RESTON, Va., Nov. 20, 2026

GKG to design and execute tailored leadership development pathways for municipal people leaders, emerging talent, and executive officers.

RESTON, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Golden Key Group (GKG), a leading provider of enterprise workforce solutions and human capital strategies, announced today that it has been selected by the City of Cleveland Department of Personnel and Human Resources to design and deliver its Citywide Management Training Program.

Under the contract, GKG will implement a comprehensive, cohort-based hybrid learning strategy aimed at driving leadership excellence across all municipal departments. The program leverages instructor-led sessions, digital LMS coursework, and applied capstone projects to strengthen core leadership competencies at every organizational tier.

"Every thriving city relies on leaders who are equipped to guide their teams through complex, evolving challenges," said Donnielle DeMesme, VP of Leadership and Development. "We are thrilled to partner with the City of Cleveland to bring our proven instructional design methodology and tailored training strategies to their workforce. This program is built to foster lasting culture change, elevate day-to-day operations, and empower Cleveland's public leaders at every stage of their career."

The GKG-designed curriculum includes three specialized tracks:

  • People Leaders Track: Supporting new and first-time managers through leadership transitions, coaching, conflict resolution, and communication.
  • Executive Leaders Track: Advancing emotional intelligence, culture building, and executive presence for directors and senior leaders.
  • Core Leadership Track: Equipping emerging leaders with essential skills in HR fundamentals, performance management, and team continuity.

This partnership highlights GKG's continued expansion in designing modern, outcome-driven learning solutions for state and local government agencies alongside its long-standing federal portfolio. Building on recent success with municipal and state initiatives including the City of Minneapolis and the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM), GKG continues to solidify its position as a trusted learning and development partner for public sector organizations nationwide.

About Golden Key Group
Golden Key Group (GKG) is a premier provider of HR solutions, specializing in human capital management, employee training and development, and workforce strategy. Dedicated to excellence, integrity, and client-driven results, GKG partners with federal, state, and local government agencies to modernize their workforce, enhance operational efficiency, and cultivate strong leadership pipelines. Through customized, high-impact solutions, GKG equips public sector organizations with the strategic expertise needed to drive long-term success in an evolving employment landscape. For more information, visit www.goldenkeygroup.com.

Debevoise Continues Private Equity M&A Expansion with the Addition of Partner Jenna McBain

Debevoise Continues Private Equity M&A Expansion with the Addition of Partner Jenna McBain

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Debevoise & Plimpton LLP announced today that Jenna McBain is joining the firm as a partner in its Mergers & Acquisitions Group in New York, adding further depth to its private equity M&A practice.

Ms. McBain advises leading sponsors and their portfolio companies on complex mergers, acquisitions and divestitures across a range of industries, with particular experience in infrastructure.

Ms. McBain's arrival follows the recent additions of partners Neal Reenan and Ian Bushner, continuing the firm's investment in its private equity M&A practice. Including Ms. McBain, Debevoise has increased its global M&A partner headcount by more than 30% in 2026.

Presiding Partner Peter Furci said, "Our private capital platform is central to the firm's strategy. Jenna brings deep transactional experience and strong sponsor relationships that will further strengthen our ability to serve clients on their most complex M&A matters."

Kevin Rinker, Co-Chair of the M&A Group, said, "Debevoise has long been a leader in private equity M&A, and Jenna's arrival adds to the exceptional depth of our team. We're seeing strong momentum across the practice, and her experience advising leading sponsors will further enhance the capabilities we bring to clients."

Ms. McBain said, "Debevoise has a leading private capital platform and a long history of advising sponsors on their most complex transactions. The firm's depth of experience, range of talent and collaborative approach make it a strong fit for my practice and clients."

Prior to joining Debevoise, Ms. McBain was a partner at Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP. She received her LL.M. from New York University School of Law in 2016, her LPC from the College of Law, London, in 2012, her GDL from BPP Law School in 2011 and her B.A. from Bristol University in 2010.

data.title: Pinnacol Assurance Wins Denver Metro Chamber's Business Impact Award for Corporate Social Responsibility
data.description:
Pinnacol Assurance Wins Denver Metro Chamber's Business Impact Award for Corporate Social Responsibility

Pinnacol Assurance Wins Denver Metro Chamber's Business Impact Award for Corporate Social Responsibility

PR Newswire

DENVER, Nov. 20, 2026

Colorado's largest workers' compensation insurer recognized for investing in families, workforce development and community nonprofits

DENVER, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce named Pinnacol Assurance as the winner of their Business Impact Award in the Corporate Social Responsibility category. The awards recognize "the businesses shaping Colorado's economy and creating a stronger future."

Pinnacol, a home-grown, member-owned workers' comp carrier that has protected Colorado workers and employers for more than 110 years, was recognized for investing in the communities it serves, from scholarships for families affected by workplace tragedy to workforce development for underrepresented Coloradans.

"Pinnacol was created to protect Colorado workers and businesses, and we believe that responsibility doesn't end when a claim closes," said Pinnacol President and CEO, John O'Donnell. "This recognition belongs to our employees, who make a difference for Colorado families, students, and small businesses. We're grateful to the Denver Metro Chamber for this recognition, and we're committed to doing even more."

"Pinnacol Assurance is a fantastic organization, and it shows in everything they do," said Raymond H. Gonzales, Executive Vice President of the Denver Metro Chamber and Interim President of the Chamber Leadership Foundation. "Their approach to corporate social responsibility isn't a side project. It's woven into how they operate, from the culture they've built for their own employees to the impact they make in communities across Colorado. That kind of commitment creates a ripple effect, spreading positivity inside the company and far beyond its walls. Pinnacol is exactly the kind of leader this award was created to celebrate."

Supporting Colorado families and workers

Through the Pinnacol Foundation, Pinnacol has awarded nearly $8 million in scholarships to more than 800 Colorado students since 2001, making it the largest program of its kind in the country. The scholarships go to children whose parents were seriously injured or killed on the job, whether or not the parent was insured by Pinnacol. In 2025-26, 86 students received more than $400,000.

Building Colorado's workforce

In 2025, 76% of Pinnacol's community investments supported workforce development in underrepresented communities. Those investments helped more than 5,700 students and adult learners pursue career pathways. Participants earned more than 5,500 credentials, and more than 650 graduates entered construction jobs.

Pinnacol also awarded $265,622 to 16 Colorado nonprofits in 2025, including the Foundation for Colorado Community Colleges, Mi Casa Resource Center, CrossPurpose and the Construction Education Foundation of Colorado.

In the last decade, Pinnacol's youth apprenticeship program has employed 83 paid apprentices from eight school districts and 24 high schools. About 30% have converted to full-time Pinnacol employees. The model has been studied by state delegations, federal policymakers and educators, and in 2025 the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment honored Pinnacol with its Creating Tomorrow's Workforce Today Award.

Employees giving back

Pinnacol employees receive unlimited paid time to volunteer. In 2025, they contributed more than 2,500 hours to 104 Colorado nonprofits, including 708 hours supporting veterans and disabled veterans. Through Pinnacol in Action, employees have given more than 80,000 volunteer hours over two decades.

Employee giving is also strong. In 2025, an astounding 82.3% of employees participated in the company's giving campaign, donating $175,044. Pinnacol matched those gifts, bringing the total to $350,089 for nonprofits serving our community.

Turning recovery into service

Pinnacol's Return to Work Volunteering Program connects injured workers who can't yet return to their regular jobs with nonprofits for modified-duty work. Participants have contributed approximately 14,000 volunteer hours across Colorado, keeping workers active and connected while nonprofits gain extra help.

data.title: AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Global Atlantic Financial Group Limited and Its Subsidiaries
data.description:
AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Global Atlantic Financial Group Limited and Its Subsidiaries

AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICR) of “a+” (Excellent) of Commonwealth Annuity and Life Insurance Company (Brighton, MA), First Allmerica Financial Life Insurance Company (Brighton, MA), Forethought Life Insurance Company (Indianapolis, IN), Accordia Life and Annuity Company (Des Moines, IA), and its affiliates, Global Atlantic Re Limited (Bermuda) and Global Atlantic Assurance Limited (Bermuda). These subsidiaries are referred to collectively as Global Atlantic Group (Global Atlantic). AM Best also has affirmed the Long-Term ICR of bbb+” (Good) of Global Atlantic Financial Group Limited (Bermuda). The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

The ratings reflect Global Atlantic’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The rating affirmations reflect Global Atlantic’s strong balance sheet strength metrics. The balance sheet strength metrics are driven by risk-adjusted capitalization that AM Best assesses at the strong level, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), appropriate level of liquidity, robust asset/liability matching program, and strong financial flexibility. The investment portfolio is composed primarily of fixed income instruments including corporate bonds, mortgage loans, structured securities and government securities. Global Atlantic has experienced double-digit growth in the group’s invested assets over the past five years. The main drivers in this growth include an increase in direct business written in the group’s individual markets, and large block/flow reinsurance transactions. The block transactions introduce some volatility in net premium growth, but the five-year trend is generally positive. AM Best notes that privately placed assets will continue to grow in the near term and are expected to benefit future yield performance. The group’s operating performance is adequate to reflect recent statutory strain and volatility. In addition, unadjusted GAAP results also show volatility in recent years. Underwriting losses continue to be offset largely by investment income. New money yields continue to produce record-high yields for the group’s portfolio. Overall earnings have been lower over the recent three-year period, particularly on a statutory basis. Premium growth is expected to remain strong with support from robust distribution channels in the individual and institutional business segments. In addition, AM Best believes the group has large pipelines of potential business on both block and flow transactions.

Global Atlantic’s favorable business profile stems partly from the group’s strategic market presence and defensible position in the annuity market. Global Atlantic has a strong market presence as evidenced by its top market share in both the individual annuity and preneed space. Global Atlantic is also the reinsurer of choice for many blue-chip counterparties and has expanded its presence in the reinsurance space domestically and internationally. The group utilizes several different structures and treaties to provide reinsurance solutions that strengthen relationships with its clients. Global Atlantic continues to utilize its sidecars, Ivy I, Ivy II, Ivy III, and Triton as co-investment vehicles. AM Best notes that Ivy I and II are fully deployed while Ivy III and Triton are still deploying capital. These sidecars help Global Atlantic in providing solutions to its reinsurance clients and provide co-investors with more investment opportunities.

Global Atlantic’s ERM program has continued to grow and adapt, meeting the needs of the group and the larger organization. The program features an integrated framework throughout the organization. In addition, robust liquidity buffers and stress testing are in place as key risk mitigation considerations. AM Best expects continued program expansion with support from KKR & Co. Inc.’s capabilities.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. For additional information regarding the use and limitations of Credit Rating opinions, please view Guide to Best's Credit Ratings. For information on the proper use of Best’s Credit Ratings, Best’s Performance Assessments, Best’s Preliminary Credit Assessments and AM Best press releases, please view Guide to Proper Use of Best’s Ratings & Assessments.

Headquartered in the United States, the company does business in over 100 countries with regional offices in London, Amsterdam, Dubai, Hong Kong, Singapore and Mexico City. data.title: OrthoLite Launches New Supercritical Foam Insole Collection for Performance Footwear at The Running Event 2026
data.description:
OrthoLite Launches New Supercritical Foam Insole Collection for Performance Footwear at The Running Event 2026

OrthoLite®, the global leader in branded, high-performance comfort footwear solutions, introduces OrthoLite® Lift™, a brand new, next-generation insole innovation that delivers lightweight comfort and high resilience by combining engineered polymer formulations with supercritical foaming technology. The new Lift collection will be unveiled at The Running Event in San Antonio, Texas Dec. 1-3, 2026.

The OrthoLite Lift collection uses supercritically foamed aliphatic TPU through a supercritical foaming process, which gives footwear brands and their factory partners a coordinated set of performance options for the footbed. The new OrthoLite Lift innovation shows the material science depth that OrthoLite brings to the industry as part of the Coats Footwear Division.

OrthoLite Lift uses supercritical foaming technology to create a consistent, refined cellular structure, delivering lightweight cushioning and high resilience. Lift expands OrthoLite’s material platform beyond its established open-cell PU technologies, giving brands greater choice in engineering comfort and performance.

Lift debuts with two formulations:

  • OrthoLite® Lift™ ATPU: Built for high-demand environments like trail running, hiking and elite athletic performance, Lift ATPU delivers exceptional lightness in a low-density construction, ≥65% resilience, better step-in comfort and abrasion resistance. Its hydrophobic, closed-cell construction resists water absorption, helping maintain structural integrity and consistent cushioning in dry and wet conditions.
  • OrthoLite® Lift™ DLT: OrthoLite Dual Layer Technology (DLT) combines a supercritically foamed ATPU base for lightweight resilience with a customizable OrthoLite open-cell PU top layer for comfort, breathability and moisture management of the insole. OrthoLite DLT is ideal for all active lifestyle footwear categories.

“Footwear brands aren’t looking for incremental gains anymore. They want material innovation they can build a product and brand story around,” said Marty Greenwald, Vice President of Sales for OrthoLite. “Lift gives brands a new material option when they need lightweight cushioning, high resilience and lasting comfort. And it’s just the latest from an innovation pipeline built on decades of OrthoLite material science.”

Attendees can explore the OrthoLite Lift insole collection at booth #21111 at The Running Event, Dec. 1-3, 2026, in San Antonio. Footwear brands and factory partners can learn more at ortholite.com.

About OrthoLite®

A division of Coats Group plc, OrthoLite® is the world's leading manufacturer and supplier of branded, high-performance, comfort footwear solutions, which the company delivers at scale while prioritizing reduced-impact manufacturing and responsible innovation. Through long-standing partnerships and industry initiatives, OrthoLite supports brands, consumers and the broader footwear ecosystem. Visit www.ortholite.com to learn more.

About Coats Group plc

Coats is a world-leading Tier 2 manufacturer and trusted partner for the apparel and footwear industries. We deliver essential materials, components, and software solutions that help our customers grow, compete and win.

With over 250 years of industry expertise, we’re shaping the future of the apparel and footwear supply chain through insight-led innovation, impactful sustainability practices, and digital technologies that unlock better product quality, efficiency and performance.

Headquartered in the UK, Coats is a FTSE 250 company and a constituent of the FTSE4Good Index. In 2025, we generated $1.5 billion in revenue and employed approximately 19,000 people worldwide – all united by a spirit of innovation, quality and service.
